1.explanation:
- aggregator/aggregate-test.js: Exercises the aggregation logic itself; this is where we expect category aggregation to fail when any child is failing.
- index-test.js: Verifies the end-to-end CLI/index behavior, including how results are reported and aggregated.
- runner-test.js: Covers the test runner’s grouping and aggregation of audits by category, where this bug manifests.
- audits/audit-test.js: Defines the base Audit contract and test fixtures, ensuring audit results conform to expectations.
- audits/accessibility/color-contrast-test.js: Implements the specific contrast-ratio audit that’s failing in the screenshot; necessary to see how a failing audit result is fed into the aggregator.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows the “Accessibility” category marked with a green check (passing) even though one of its child audits (“Background and foreground colors have a sufficient contrast ratio”) has a red X (failure). In other words, the aggregator that rolls up individual audit results into their parent category is incorrectly marking the overall category as passing when at least one sub-audit has failed. To reproduce, run the accessibility audits (including the color-contrast audit) and observe that a failing sub-audit still yields a passing category aggregation.
